title: Add retry logic to event ingestion pipeline with exponential backoff
body:
Implement exponential backoff for transient failures in the event ingestion worker. Currently, failed batches are dropped after a single attempt, causing data loss during brief network partitions or downstream service restarts.

Changes:
- Add configurable retry queue with exponential backoff (base 2, max 5 attempts)
- Track retry count and last attempt timestamp in event metadata
- Emit retry metrics to observability backend for visibility

Tested:
- Unit tests verify backoff intervals (100ms, 200ms, 400ms, 800ms, 1600ms)
- Integration test confirms 100 events survive a 30-second service downtime
- Verified no duplicate events on successful retry

Remaining risk: Ingestion lag may increase during sustained outages if retry queue grows unbounded. Monitor queue depth metric post-deploy.

title: Reconcile billing ledger with metered usage for October cycle
body:
Align billing system's recorded usage against metered event counts from analytics pipeline. October reconciliation shows 2.3% variance (likely rounding and clock skew).

Changes:
- Add ledger comparison report that groups discrepancies by customer and hour
- Implement tolerance threshold (±3%) before flagging for manual review
- Add reconciliation run timestamp and hash to audit trail

Tested:
- Reconciliation report generated for September (known clean) shows 0.1% variance
- Manual spot-check of 5 high-volume customers confirms metered counts match
- Report output validated against schema

Remaining risk: Customers with custom billing rules or credit adjustments may show larger variance. Review flagged accounts before publishing final October invoice.

title: Fix dashboard filter state persistence across page navigation
body:
Dashboard filters (date range, customer segment, metric type) were not persisting when users navigated between views and returned. Filters reset to defaults, requiring re-entry.

Changes:
- Store active filter state in browser URL query parameters
- Deserialize filter state on page load and restore to form inputs
- Add change handler to update URL on filter modification
- Preserve filter state across browser back/forward navigation

Tested:
- Manual verification: set filters, navigate to different page, return—filters restored
- Tested with 6-month date range and multiple segment selections
- Verified URL remains clean when no filters applied (no query string)
- Browser back button correctly restores previous filter state

Remaining risk: Very long filter URLs (many segments) may exceed browser limits on some clients. Consider compression or session storage fallback if needed.

title: Adjust report drawer layout for improved mobile responsiveness
body:
Report detail drawer was unusable on mobile devices: buttons overlapped, text wrapping broke, and close button was inaccessible. This blocked mobile users from viewing report details.

Changes:
- Convert drawer to full-screen modal on viewports below 768px
- Stack action buttons vertically and increase touch target to 44px minimum
- Adjust font sizing and line-height for readability on small screens
- Move close button to top-right corner with adequate padding

Tested:
- Verified layout on 390px phone, 768px tablet, and desktop (1440px) viewports
- Tested all buttons are tappable without accidental adjacent taps
- Confirmed text remains readable at standard mobile zoom levels
- Tested drawer open/close animation remains smooth on lower-end devices

Remaining risk: Devices with notches or safe areas may have layout issues. Monitor error reports from mobile users post-deploy.

title: Correct health check endpoint path in monitoring configuration
body:
Monitoring system was configured to probe `/healthz` but the application exposes `/health`. This caused false-positive alerts during normal operation and masked real issues.

Changes:
- Update monitoring agent configuration to probe `/health` endpoint
- Verify endpoint returns 200 and valid JSON schema
- Add integration test to confirm monitoring can reach health endpoint

Tested:
- Confirmed `/health` endpoint responds with 200 and expected JSON
- Verified `/healthz` returns 404 (no longer used)
- Monitoring agent successfully connects to corrected endpoint
- Health check latency under 100ms

Remaining risk: Any external monitoring systems using `/healthz` will need manual reconfiguration. Coordinate with operations team before deploy.

title: Round cart totals to nearest cent and fix currency display formatting
body:
Shopping cart totals were displaying with floating-point precision artifacts (e.g., $99.99000000001). This caused customer confusion and failed validation in billing system.

Changes:
- Round cart subtotal, tax, and final total to 2 decimal places using banker's rounding
- Apply currency formatting consistently across all cart views (summary, checkout, receipt)
- Add validation to reject orders where calculated total differs from displayed total by >$0.01

Tested:
- Unit tests verify rounding for common tax rates (6%, 8%, 10%)
- Tested cart with 3, 15, and 47 line items—all totals round correctly
- Manual verification: $99.99000000001 now displays as $99.99
- Billing system accepts all test orders without rejection

Remaining risk: Existing orders with display-total mismatches may need manual review. Check reconciliation report for any affected customers.

title: Retry ingestion pipeline on transient database connection errors
body:
Add exponential backoff retry logic to the data ingestion worker when it encounters connection timeouts or temporary unavailability from the warehouse. Previously, a single connection hiccup would fail the entire batch.

Implementation uses a max of 5 retries with 2-second base delay, doubling on each attempt. Retries only trigger on specific error codes (connection refused, timeout, deadlock). Permanent errors (auth failure, schema mismatch) fail fast without retry.

Tested against staging warehouse with network fault injection. Verified that 3-second outages are now absorbed without batch loss. Metrics show retry counts and success rates are logged for monitoring.

Risk: Retry loop could mask persistent configuration issues if error classification is incomplete. Requires monitoring of retry rates in production to catch misconfiguration early.

title: Fix billing reconciliation query to handle partial-month prorations correctly
body:
Correct the month-end billing reconciliation report to account for mid-cycle subscription changes. Previously, prorated charges were being double-counted when a customer upgraded or downgraded mid-month.

The reconciliation query now groups charges by billing period window and sums prorated amounts only once per customer per calendar month. Added a date range filter to ensure clean boundaries between billing cycles.

Validated against 6 months of historical test data with synthetic upgrade/downgrade events. Report totals now match the expected revenue ledger within rounding tolerance. Added unit tests for edge cases (same-day upgrade, month-boundary transitions).

Risk: Historical reports may need restatement if prior months had undetected double-counts. Recommend running a one-time audit query against production data before deploying to live billing.

title: Add dataset size filter to analytics dashboard
body:
Extend the dashboard filter panel to let users filter query results by dataset size ranges (small, medium, large, extra-large). Improves performance for users analyzing specific workload categories and reduces cognitive load when exploring large result sets.

Filter state is persisted in URL query parameters so users can share filtered views. Implemented as a multi-select dropdown with predefined thresholds. Backend applies the filter at the query layer before aggregation.

Tested with datasets spanning 1 MB to 50 GB. Filter application reduces average query latency by 15–40% depending on the selected range. Verified that filter state survives page reload and browser back-button navigation.

Risk: Thresholds are hardcoded and may need adjustment as data growth patterns shift. Consider moving to a configuration table in future work if threshold tuning becomes frequent.

title: Adjust report drawer height to prevent content cutoff on smaller viewports
body:
Modify the report detail drawer CSS to use viewport-relative sizing instead of fixed pixel heights. On tablets and smaller laptops, the drawer was clipping the bottom sections of long reports.

Changed from `max-height: 600px` to `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px)` to leave breathing room for header and footer. Added overflow scrolling within the drawer body. Tested responsive behavior at breakpoints 768px, 1024px, 1440px, and 2560px.

Verified that all report sections remain accessible and readable on a tablet and 13-inch laptop screens. Text is no longer truncated and scrolling is smooth. Layout passes accessibility audit for touch target sizes.

Risk: Very tall reports on small screens will now require scrolling, which could be initially disorienting. Mitigated by adding a sticky section header so users always see the report title while scrolling.

title: Implement cart total rounding to nearest cent
body:
Apply banker's rounding (round-half-to-even) to cart totals to eliminate fractional-cent discrepancies that accumulate across line items. Previously, line-item prices summed to amounts like $99.999 or $100.001 due to floating-point arithmetic.

Rounding is applied at the final total calculation step, after all discounts and taxes. Uses a dedicated utility function to ensure consistent behavior across web and API surfaces. All monetary amounts are stored as integers (cents) in the database.

Tested with 500 synthetic carts containing 1–50 items with various tax rates and discounts. All totals now round to exact cents. Verified that rounding direction matches accounting standards and does not systematically favor customer or merchant.

Risk: Existing carts in the database may have fractional-cent totals. Recommend a data migration to normalize historical records, or accept that legacy carts will display the old totals until they are re-calculated.

title: Standardize API health check endpoint path
body:
Rename the health check endpoint from `/healthz` to `/health` to match common conventions and reduce confusion among monitoring integrations. The old path was inconsistent with documentation and load balancer expectations.

The new `/health` endpoint returns a 200 OK response with a JSON body containing service status, database connectivity, and cache availability. The old `/healthz` path now issues a 301 redirect to `/health` for backward compatibility during a deprecation window.

Tested with staging load balancer and monitoring agents. All probes now succeed and correctly identify service availability. Redirect adds negligible latency (<1 ms). Verified that concurrent requests to both paths work correctly.

Risk: Clients using the old path will experience a one-request delay due to redirect. Recommend a communication period before removing the redirect path. Monitor logs for residual `/healthz` traffic to ensure migration is complete.
